name: Cruachan

attributes.attribute: an Irish mythological site with many variant names

sources: Dames, Michael. Mythic Ireland. London: Thames and Hudson, 1992, 237–242.
Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Vol. III. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, 349–355.
Hull, Eleanor. The Cuchullin Saga in Irish Literature. London: David Nutt, 1898, 111+.

text: Cruachan is the great fortress of Connacht in the saga literature. Its names include Crogan, Rathcrogan, Cruachain, Crúachu, Rathcruachain, and Bri Ele. Irish titles add Uaimh Chrúachan, the cave, and Druim na nDruadh, the druids' ridge. The Táin Bó Cuailnge makes it the seat of queen Medb and king Ailill. The story-site is identified with Rathcroghan near Tulsk in north Co. Roscommon. In age and in the number of its mentions it ranks with the royal sites of Ireland. Tara, Emain Macha, and Dún Ailinne are its peers. The writers picture a splendid and sprawling stronghold with seven compartments. It became a byword for the wealth and power of the west province. Its cave is called the Hells Gate of Ireland. The Echtra Nerai makes that cave a place of horror. From it issue the devastator Aillén. White birds whose breath withered all growth came out of it, three cats of prey, and wild pigs beyond counting. Archaeologists read Rathcroghan as a capital the Goidelic invaders built. They used it to hold the native people down. The site covers about two miles square. It carries earthworks of many kinds, mounds that may be passage graves, and five rings of fortified ground. Amateur names such as Medb's Treasury and Medb's Mill cling to its points. Reiligna Righ, the Cemetery of the Kings, proved on excavation to hold no burials. A standing stone seven feet high marks the grave of king Dathi. Ogham inscriptions run at several places on the site.

okr.objective: Cruachan is the mythological site and capital of Connacht associated with the queen Medb.
key_results: Cruachan is named an Irish mythological site.
It stands in the eastern part of the western province of Connacht.
It is also called Crogan, Rathcrogan, Cruachain, Crúachu, Rathcruachain, and Bri Ele.
MacKillop heads the fortress article with the forms Cruachain and Cruachan and adds Uaimh Chrúachan and Druim na nDruadh.
The Táin Bó Cuailnge makes it the seat of Medb and Ailill, counterpart of Tara, Emain Macha, and Dún Ailinne.
The cave called the Hells Gate of Ireland issues Aillén, withering birds, predatory cats, and countless pigs.
Excavation showed Reiligna Righ was no burial place, and ogham inscriptions run across the site.
